transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I guess… it’s mostly that I’m not taking things in like I should. My wife will be telling me about, you know, my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’ll be looking right at her, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really catch half of what she said.
Has this trouble taking in what people say been something you've noticed since childhood or your younger years, or did it start more recently in your life?

Yeah… I think it goes back pretty far. In grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was smart enough, but I’d be off daydreaming, or I’d leave homework in my desk. They had to remind me a lot to finish things in class.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have off days, but I haven’t really noticed being down or not enjoying things lately.

Aside from these longstanding attention issues, have you noticed any new or worsening problems with your memory recently—like forgetting familiar names, getting lost in places you know well, or losing track of the date or time?
Not really, no. I mean, I misplace things or miss what someone said, but I haven’t noticed anything like getting lost or forgetting who people are.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with longstanding, pervasive inattentive symptoms (poor listening, forgetting instructions, leaving tasks unfinished, daydreaming) beginning before age 12 as reported by childhood teacher feedback, with functional impact on daily communication and task completion in adulthood. No evidence of depressive episode, mood disturbance, or acquired cognitive decline (memory loss, disorientation) that would suggest an alternative diagnosis such as major depressive disorder or a neurocognitive disorder. Symptom pattern and childhood onset are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, unspecified type.
